title: SHE DESTROYED TWO KINGDOMS
subtitle: the nine-tailed fox, before Japan
source: Edo-period legend of the nine-tailed fox (Takai Ranzan & Hokusai, Ehon Sankoku Yofuden, 1803-05; earlier Tamamo-no-Mae tales): Daji of Shang (Fengshen Yanyi / Shiji), Lady Kayo of India, Bao Si of Zhou (Shiji beacon-fire story), voyage to Japan on Kibi no Makibi's envoy ship (753), Tamamo-no-Mae at Emperor Toba's court, Sessho-seki at Nasu (split March 2022).

lines.say: [ominous] Before this fox was sealed inside a killing stone in Japan... she had already destroyed two kingdoms.
cap: Before this fox was {r:sealed in stone}

lines.say: [storytelling] Three thousand years ago in China, she became Daji, the queen of King Zhou.
She filled a pool with wine, hung meat from the trees, and threw a party that never ended.
[darker] Anyone who complained was forced to walk across a red-hot bronze pillar.
The people rebelled. The dynasty fell. And the queen... vanished.
[sly] India. As Lady Kayo, a prince's wife. She made him behead a thousand men.
[beat] But here's where it gets weird. She went back to China.
As Bao Si, a queen who never smiled. So the king lit the war beacons, just to make her laugh.
cap: So the king lit the {r:war beacons}

lines.say: [quiet] She laughed. So he did it again, and again. Then a real army came... and nobody answered the fires.
cap: So he did it {o:again}... and again.

lines.say: Then she became a young girl, and slipped aboard a ship to Japan.
[storytelling] Four hundred years later, she was Tamamo-no-Mae, the most beautiful woman at court.
Until a court diviner saw her shadow. Nine tails.
[worried] And that's how she ended up in the rock.
[sly] The rock that split in half in twenty twenty-two.
[ominous, quiet] Nobody knows. But I know where she started.
